slides.title: Why Measuring Medical Affairs Is Different
bullets: Commercial results show up directly in sales figures
Medical Affairs value shows up in harder-to-quantify dimensions
Relationship quality, clinical understanding, and contribution to practice
This requires a deliberately different measurement approach

slides.title: KPIs Must Align with Strategy, Not Just Count Activity
bullets: Current frameworks insist KPIs must align with medical strategy
Counting MSL visits measures activity, not strategic contribution
The literature flags this as one of the most common measurement traps

slides.title: Activity and Interaction Metrics
bullets: Qualified interactions and coverage of priority stakeholders
Still relevant, but only as indicators of process
Never the final goal of the measurement system on their own

slides.title: Quality, Insight, and Scientific Impact
bullets: Insight quality is measured by whether insights drove real decisions
Not by how many insights were logged
Publication quality is measured by journal impact factor and citations
Not simply by the number of publications produced

slides.title: Outcome-Based KPIs
bullets: Observable changes in clinical practice or appropriate treatment adoption
Patient health outcomes attributable, even indirectly, to medical activity
The most advanced and most demanding level of medical measurement

slides.title: Isolating Medical Affairs' Real Contribution
bullets: Many factors influence clinical practice and health outcomes at once
Isolating the specific contribution of Medical Affairs is methodologically complex
Requires combining quantitative metrics with well-documented qualitative evidence

slides.title: Understanding the System Behind the Numbers
bullets: Goes beyond the routine activity figures you report day to day
Lets you argue the real value of your work with both data and narrative
Sets up the module's next lesson on the medical impact narrative

takeaway.title: A mature KPI system moves from counting activity to demonstrating real impact
bullets: Activity metrics are process indicators, not the end goal
Insight and publication quality matter more than raw counts
Outcome-based KPIs are the hardest to prove but the most valuable
